From 95171e45663307fc33a939f0220b39afadfe7cb9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Date: Thu, 14 Dec 2023 18:39:31 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] mei: fix vsc dependency

CONFIG_INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW can be set to built-in even with CONFIG_MEI=m,
but then the driver is not built because Kbuild never enters the
drivers/misc/mei directory for built-in files, leading to a link
failure:

ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_reset" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_init" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_xfer" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_need_read" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_enable" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_synchronize" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_intr_disable" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!
ERROR: modpost: "vsc_tp_register_event_cb" [drivers/misc/mei/mei-vsc.ko] undefined!

Add an explicit dependency on CONFIG_MEI that was apparently missing,
to ensure the VSC_HW driver cannot be built-in with MEI itself being
a loadable module.

Fixes: 566f5ca97680 ("mei: Add transport driver for IVSC device")
Signed-off-by: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Reviewed-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Wentong Wu <wentong.wu@intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231214183946.109124-1-arnd@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig b/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
index 858bd701d68c..1e28ca23a74a 100644
--- a/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig
@@ -62,6 +62,7 @@ config INTEL_MEI_GSC
 
 config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
 	tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
 	depends on ACPI && SPI
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST
 	help
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/misc/mei/Kconfig`**
   - Added a new dependency line: `depends on INTEL_MEI` for the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` configuration option.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the `Kconfig` file establishes a dependency that ensures the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver cannot be built as a built-in module if the `CONFIG_MEI` option is set to be a loadable module. This change addresses a linking issue that arose when the driver was built without the necessary dependencies, leading to undefined references during the build process. The fix is aimed at preventing future build failures related to the `vsc` transport driver for the Intel visual sensing controller.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of an explicit dependency on `CONFIG_MEI` for the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver in the Kconfig file. This allowed the driver to be built as a built-in module even when `CONFIG_MEI` was set to be a loadable module, leading to undefined references during the linking process because the necessary components were not included.

Here is the patch:
 config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
 	tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
 	depends on ACPI && SPI
 	depends on GPIOLIB || COMPILE_TEST

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```plaintext
config INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW
tristate "Intel visual sensing controller device transport driver"
```
Reason:
The absence of an explicit dependency on `CONFIG_MEI` for the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver allows it to be built as a built-in module even when `CONFIG_MEI` is set to be a loadable module. This results in undefined references during the linking process because the necessary components from `CONFIG_MEI` are not included.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
+	depends on INTEL_MEI
```
Reason:
Adding the line `depends on INTEL_MEI` creates an explicit dependency that ensures the `INTEL_MEI_VSC_HW` driver cannot be built-in unless `CONFIG_MEI` is also built-in. This prevents the situation where the driver is built without the necessary components, thus resolving the undefined reference errors during the linking process.
